questions.question: What makes a good alt attribute, and when should it be empty?
questions.answer: Alt should describe the image's purpose or information, not its filename or appearance. Decorative images use alt="" so screen readers skip them; functional images inside links/buttons describe the action.

questions.question: Why set width and height on img, and how does CSS still make it responsive?
questions.answer: The attributes give the browser an aspect ratio to reserve space before loading, preventing layout shift (CLS). CSS such as width:100%; height:auto can still scale the image while the ratio is preserved.

questions.question: Explain srcset/sizes versus picture/source.
questions.answer: srcset with sizes lets the browser choose an image resolution based on viewport and device pixel ratio. picture with source is for art direction or format fallback (AVIF/WebP), and must end with a fallback img.

questions.question: What are the requirements for accessible audio and video?
questions.answer: Show controls, provide captions via track for speech, include transcript/fallback content, avoid autoplaying sound, and add a poster for video. Keep media keyboard operable through native controls.

questions.question: Write a responsive, lazy-loaded figure for Kakade's desk photo with a caption.
Embed Kakade's talk video with captions and a fallback message.
questions.answer:
<video controls width="640" height="360" poster="/img/kakade-poster.jpg">
  <source src="/media/kakade-talk.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
  <track kind="captions" src="/media/kakade-talk.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default />
  Your browser does not support video.
</video>

questions.question: Why is alt="kakade-photo.jpg" considered harmful?
questions.answer: It repeats the filename rather than describing the content, so screen-reader users hear meaningless noise. Use a description of what the image conveys, or alt="" if it is decorative.

questions.question: An image causes the whole article to jump when it loads. What did the author forget?
questions.answer: Width and height attributes (or an aspect-ratio), so the browser could not reserve space and reflowed the page after the image loaded. Add intrinsic dimensions and let CSS scale responsively.
